definitions.explanation: A flat, folding wallet designed primarily for holding paper currency, as distinguished from coin purses or general-purpose wallets.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{札入|さつい}れを{買|か}った。
{札入|さつい}れに{一万円札|いちまんえんさつ}が{三枚|さんまい}{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: There are three 10,000-yen bills in my billfold.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}に{革|かわ}の{札入|さつい}れをプレゼントした。
examples.english: I gave my father a leather billfold for his birthday.

notes:
A compound of {札|さつ} (banknote, bill) and {入|い}れ (container, holder). Refers specifically to the flat, folding type of wallet designed primarily for holding paper money. Distinguished from coin purses and more general wallets.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {革|かわ}の{札入|さつい}れ: leather billfold
- {長|なが}{札入|さつい}れ: long wallet
- {二|ふた}つ{折|お}りの{札入|さつい}れ: bi-fold wallet

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {財布|さいふ}: wallet, purse — the general and most common term; can hold bills, coins, and cards
- {小銭入|こぜにい}れ: coin purse — specifically for coins
- {長財布|ながさいふ}: long wallet — the modern common term for a wallet that holds bills flat
